root_cause.text: The AMD ISP DesignWare I2C platform probe enabled runtime PM and used `pm_runtime_get_sync()` before `i2c_dw_probe()`, which could trigger an early runtime-resume of the same `amdisp` device via genpd before probe initialization completed, causing a resume-probe race and NULL dereference.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says `pm_runtime_get_sync()` “before i2c_dw_probe() triggers PM resume, which powers on ISP and also invokes the amdisp i2c runtime resume before the probe completes resulting in this race condition and a NULL dereferencing issue,” and the patch removes that sequence, replacing it with direct `dev_pm_genpd_resume()/suspend()`, then `pm_runtime_set_suspended()` and delayed `pm_runtime_enable()` after `i2c_dw_probe()` finishes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the pm_domain header to enable power-domain support in this source file.
intent_record.what: A new header include, <linux/pm_domain.h>, was added alongside the existing Linux kernel includes.
intent_record.how: This change makes power-domain related APIs, types, or declarations available to the translation unit so the code can use PM domain functionality at compile time; it does not by itself alter runtime logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Adjust probe-time power management to use genpd resume/suspend sequencing and leave the device in a suspended runtime PM state after initialization.
intent_record.what: In `amd_isp_dw_i2c_plat_probe()`, the code removed the initial `pm_runtime_enable()` and `pm_runtime_get_sync()` calls before `i2c_dw_probe()`, replaced them with `dev_pm_genpd_resume(&pdev->dev)`, and after a successful probe added `dev_pm_genpd_suspend(&pdev->dev)`, `pm_runtime_set_suspended(&pdev->dev)`, and `pm_runtime_enable(&pdev->dev)`. In the error path, it removed the `pm_runtime_put_sync(&pdev->dev)` cleanup call.
intent_record.how: The device is now explicitly resumed through generic power domain management only for the duration of `i2c_dw_probe()`, then returned to a suspended runtime PM state before runtime PM is enabled. This changes probe-time power handling so the driver no longer relies on a runtime PM get/put sequence during initialization and instead leaves the device suspended after setup, reducing the chance of mismatched runtime PM state during probe failure or completion.

Adjust probe-time power management to use genpd resume/suspend sequencing and leave the device in a suspended runtime PM state after initialization.

relevance_review.reason: This change only adds a pm_domain header to enable power-domain support. It does not address the runtime PM ordering issue, the premature pm_runtime_get_sync() call, or the resume-probe race that caused the NULL dereference.

The change directly targets probe-time power management sequencing, matching the root cause where runtime PM was enabled too early and caused an early resume/probe race. Leaving the device suspended after initialization avoids the problematic pm_runtime_get_sync() behavior.

candidates.rationale: This enables runtime PM and immediately resumes the device before i2c_dw_probe() completes, which can trigger an early genpd/runtime-resume of the same amdisp device and cause the resume-probe race described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement enables and immediately resumes runtime PM during probe, before i2c_dw_probe() has finished initializing the device. That early resume can re-enter the same amdisp device via genpd and trigger the resume-probe race and NULL dereference described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The probe clearly enables runtime PM and immediately forces a runtime resume before the device is fully initialized: `pm_runtime_enable(&pdev->dev);` followed by `pm_runtime_get_sync(&pdev->dev);` and only then `ret = i2c_dw_probe(isp_i2c_dev);`. This matches the reported root cause, where an early runtime-resume of the same `amdisp` device can occur before probe initialization completes, creating a resume-probe race. The runtime-resume callback dereferences driver data and can call into initialization paths (`struct dw_i2c_dev *i_dev = dev_get_drvdata(dev);` and `if (i_dev->init) i_dev->init(i_dev);`), so the vulnerable construct is present. There is no fix here to defer or avoid the early resume; no guard prevents runtime resume from running before `i2c_dw_probe()` finishes, so `is_fixed` is false.
